stories.title: Arista patches new VeloCloud Orchestrator zero-day exploited in attacks
stories.summary: Arista Networks released security updates to patch an actively exploited zero-day vulnerability affecting VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO) On-Prem deployments.
stories.explanation: Arista Networks released patches for a zero-day vulnerability (a previously unknown security flaw) in VeloCloud Orchestrator that attackers were already actively exploiting in real attacks. This matters because organizations using this on-premises version are at immediate risk of being compromised before they patch. Defenders need to apply these patches urgently and check logs to see if the vulnerability was exploited on their systems before the update was released.

stories.title: China-Linked Hackers Use ARTEX AI Agents in ConnectWise Supply Chain Attack
stories.summary: Microsoft on Wednesday disclosed that a China state-aligned actor dubbed Storm-0940 was behind the recent supply chain compromise of the ConnectWise Cloud Backup application. During the incident, Storm-0940 used ARTEX, a Go-based agentic AI penetration testing framework that was made closed-source in the wake of its abuse in cyber attacks targeting South Korean financial institutions, to speed
stories.explanation: A Chinese state-affiliated hacking group called Storm-0940 compromised ConnectWise's Cloud Backup software through its supply chain (meaning they hacked the software vendor, not individual users) and used an AI-based penetration testing tool called ARTEX to explore victim networks. This matters because it affects many organizations that trusted ConnectWise, and shows attackers are using AI automation to move faster through compromised systems. Defenders need to check if they use ConnectWise, apply any available fixes immediately, review their backup systems for unauthorized access, and monitor for signs of AI-based reconnaissance tools being used in their networks.

stories.title: ThreatsDay: AI Secrets Leak, PingCAP Source Theft, Signal Hang-Up Flaw, Laravel Auth Bypass + 21 More
stories.summary: This week has already been rough for cybersecurity. Critical PHP and GitLab RCE flaws, serious Linux security bugs, compromised eMudhra certificates, a Node.js RCE flaw, a hacked LiteLLM release, and hundreds of hijacked Tor relays. That's a lot to deal with in just a few days. And the week isn't even over yet. But those big headlines are only half the story. Stolen passwords, exposed
stories.explanation: Multiple critical vulnerabilities were disclosed in a single week across popular software including PHP, GitLab, Linux, Node.js, and others, plus compromised security certificates and hijacked network infrastructure. This matters because defenders face overwhelming work when many serious flaws drop at once, creating a backlog of patching and validation. Teams should prioritize based on what software they actually use, apply patches in order of risk to their environment, and consider temporarily restricting access to affected systems while waiting to patch.

stories.title: 11 Million Impacted by Capcom Data Breach
stories.summary: The hackers stole 11 million email addresses from CAPCOM ID and changed the login passwords for 196 accounts.
stories.explanation: Hackers stole email addresses from Capcom's gaming membership service (CAPCOM ID) affecting 11 million users and changed passwords on 196 accounts, likely to lock legitimate users out or use those accounts for further attacks. This matters because exposed email addresses can be used for targeted phishing, password spraying (trying the same password across many accounts), or sold on criminal forums. Defenders at Capcom need to notify affected users, force password resets, and investigate how the breach occurred to prevent it happening again.

stories.title: Capcom confirms data breach affecting 11.7 million accounts
stories.summary: Japanese gaming giant Capcom has confirmed that hackers breached its membership service, CAPCOM ID, exposing more than 11.7 million customer email addresses and associated information.
stories.explanation: Capcom confirmed that more than 11.7 million customer records were stolen from their CAPCOM ID membership service, exposing email addresses and associated account information. This matters because large-scale data exposure puts many customers at risk of identity theft, phishing, and account takeover attacks. Defenders and the company must notify all affected users, provide credit monitoring support, and conduct a full investigation to understand how attackers got in and what data was actually taken.

stories.title: Machine speed attacks require machine speed detection and response
stories.summary: Attackers can steal credentials and begin exfiltrating data within minutes, often before security teams can respond. Exaforce examines real-world attacks involving stolen GitHub tokens, malicious AI installers, and MFA phishing, explaining why faster detection and automated containment are critical.
stories.explanation: Attackers can now move so fast through compromised systems (stealing credentials and copying files within minutes) that traditional security teams cannot respond in time using manual processes. This matters because the speed advantage means attackers often succeed before security tools even alert defenders. Organizations need to implement automated responses (like immediately revoking stolen credentials or isolating compromised machines) and improve their detection speed through better monitoring and alert prioritization.

stories.title: Attackers Exploit Third VeloCloud Orchestrator Zero-Day in Four Months
stories.summary: The critical-severity SQL injection flaw allows attackers to access privileged internal functionality and gain operator privileges.
stories.explanation: A third critical zero-day vulnerability in VeloCloud Orchestrator was discovered within four months, this time a SQL injection flaw (a coding mistake that lets attackers run unauthorized database commands) that allows attackers to gain administrative operator privileges. This matters because the repeated discovery of serious flaws in the same product suggests deeper security issues in how it was built. Defenders using VeloCloud should treat this as urgent, apply patches immediately, and consider whether they trust this vendor enough to continue using it.

stories.title: Two CVSS 9.0 Linux KSMBD RCE Flaws Disclosed on Public Mailing Lists Before Kernel Fixes
stories.summary: Linux servers running KSMBD, the kernel's built-in SMB server, are exposed to two publicly reported remote code execution flaws rated 9.0 by Trend Micro's Zero Day Initiative, with no fix yet in the mainline kernel. One of them, ZDI-CAN-33774, can be triggered before any network authentication. The other, ZDI-CAN-33549, requires the SMB Direct transport and an RDMA-capable network
stories.explanation: Two severe remote code execution flaws (rated 9.0 out of 10 in severity) were publicly disclosed in KSMBD, a Linux file-sharing server built into the kernel, before security fixes were available in the official Linux code. One flaw can be exploited before even authenticating, meaning attackers need no valid login credentials. This matters because any Linux server using KSMBD is potentially vulnerable and there's no official patch yet, creating a gap where attackers can attack systems faster than fixes can be deployed. Defenders should disable KSMBD if not needed, isolate affected systems, and monitor carefully for exploitation attempts.

cves.name: Ahsay AhsayCBS Command Injection Vulnerability
cves.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.
cves.explanation: CVE-2026-105134 is a command injection vulnerability in Ahsay AhsayCBS (a backup management system), meaning attackers can inject unauthorized system commands that execute with the application's privileges. This matters because backup systems often have broad access to data and infrastructure, so compromising them could expose or destroy critical backups. Defenders need to apply vendor patches, review who can access this system, and check backup logs for suspicious activity.

Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.
cves.explanation: CVE-2026-104935 is an authentication bypass flaw in Ivanti Connect Secure (a remote access product) where attackers can spoof their identity to bypass login protections without needing valid credentials. This matters because remote access products are high-value targets—compromising one gives attackers direct entry to an organization's network. Defenders must patch immediately, force password resets, review who accessed the system recently, and strengthen additional security layers like IP restrictions.

cves.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.
cves.explanation: CVE-2026-21589 affects multiple Atlassian products and allows unauthorized external parties to access files or directories they shouldn't be able to reach due to improper access controls. This matters because Atlassian tools often store sensitive code, documentation, and configuration data, so exposing directories could leak valuable information. Defenders need to patch, audit what files external users could access, change any compromised credentials, and review user access permissions.

cves.explanation: CVE-2026-105133 is an improper authentication flaw in Ahsay AhsayCBS where the system fails to correctly verify user identity before granting access to sensitive backup data. This matters because it could allow unauthorized users to access, modify, or delete backups that organizations rely on for recovery. Defenders must patch this immediately, audit recent access to the system, reset credentials for users with administrative roles, and verify backup integrity.

cves.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.
cves.explanation: CVE-2026-76519 is a path traversal vulnerability in Cisco Secure Email Gateway where attackers can manipulate file paths to access files and directories outside the intended restricted areas by using relative paths like '../../../'. This matters because email gateways protect against malware and data loss, so compromising one could allow attackers to bypass security controls. Defenders need to apply patches, review email logs for suspicious file access patterns, and verify the gateway's security settings are correctly configured.
